**Observations from the image:**

- **Host plant**: Wheat (*Triticum aestivum*) — narrow leaves, characteristic stem nodes, and plant architecture confirm this.
- **Affected part**: Leaf blade (prominent foreground leaf and others visible).
- **Symptom pattern**: Irregular pale yellow-green to whitish streaking/mottling running **parallel to the leaf veins**, creating a mosaic-like interweaving of light and normal-green tissue along the length of the leaf.
- **Absence of**: Pustules (ruling out rust diseases), powdery white coating (ruling out powdery mildew), discrete brown lesions with yellow halos (ruling out Septoria or Tan Spot), distinct water-soaked/dark streaks (ruling out bacterial streak diseases).

**Reasoning:**

The hallmark symptom here is the **mosaic streaking pattern** — alternating pale yellow/white and green stripes running longitudinally along the leaf. This is the classic presentation of **Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus (WSMV)**, transmitted by the wheat curl mite. The irregular, interspersed light and dark green banding along the veins, without any pustules or necrotic lesions, strongly points to this viral disease rather than fungal or bacterial causes. Barley Yellow Dwarf Virus would show more uniform tip yellowing/reddening, and Cephalosporium Stripe would present as one or two distinct pale stripes rather than a diffuse mosaic.
